questions.stem: In chemistry, what does the term 'pure substance' mean?

options.text: A substance that is natural and unprocessed
A substance that contains only one type of element or compound
A substance that is safe to consume
A substance that has been filtered

questions.explanation: In chemistry, a pure substance contains only one type of element or compound. This is different from the everyday meaning of 'pure', which may just mean uncontaminated.

questions.stem: How can you test whether a substance is pure?

options.text: By checking if it dissolves in water
By measuring its melting or boiling point and comparing to known values
By looking at its colour
By weighing it

questions.explanation: A pure substance has a sharp, fixed melting and boiling point. If these match the known values, the substance is pure. Impure substances melt and boil over a range of temperatures.

questions.stem: What effect do impurities have on the melting point of a substance?

options.text: They increase the melting point and make it sharper
They decrease the melting point and broaden the melting range
They have no effect on the melting point
They make the substance melt at exactly 0°C

questions.explanation: Impurities lower the melting point and cause the substance to melt over a range of temperatures rather than at a sharp, fixed point.

options.text: A pure substance with no impurities
A mixture that has been designed as a useful product with specific proportions of components
A chemical equation showing reactants and products
A method for separating mixtures

questions.explanation: A formulation is a mixture that has been carefully designed to have specific properties, with each component present in a measured quantity. Examples include medicines, paints, and alloys.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a formulation?

options.text: Pure water
A single crystal of sodium chloride
An alloy such as steel
A single element like gold

questions.explanation: Steel is a formulation because it is a carefully designed mixture of iron and carbon (and sometimes other elements) in specific proportions to give desired properties.

questions.stem: What effect do impurities have on the boiling point of a substance?

options.text: They lower the boiling point
They increase the boiling point and broaden the boiling range
They have no effect on the boiling point
They cause the substance to boil at exactly 100°C

questions.explanation: Impurities increase the boiling point of a substance and cause it to boil over a range of temperatures, rather than at a single fixed temperature.

questions.stem: Pure water boils at exactly 100°C at standard pressure. A sample of water boils between 100°C and 103°C. What can you conclude?

options.text: The water is pure
The thermometer is faulty
The water contains dissolved impurities
The water is at a different pressure

questions.explanation: A pure substance boils at a fixed, sharp temperature. The fact that this sample boils over a range (100-103°C) and above the expected 100°C indicates it contains dissolved impurities.
